Use case: ui-mockup. Create realistic, production-quality UI design with clear hierarchy, readable typography and purposeful spacing. This is one independent design concept for Buildo's procedural building editor, named "Grouped inspector". It is a research concept, not a screenshot of implemented functionality.
Target dimensions: 1600 x 1128, landscape desktop application, app content only. Do not include browser/device chrome. Current date anchor 2026-10-18; no dates need to appear.
Reference image 1 is the actual Buildo app. Use its existing off-white and pale sage surfaces, dark forest-green primary actions, restrained rust secondary color, plain system sans type, thin dividers and restrained rectangular form controls. Preserve the reference's three-storey red-brick rectangular building, repeated pale window frames, modeled cornice and dark green entrance, seen in three-quarter perspective on a neutral ground. Do not beautify the building into a different or more advanced architectural result. The variation is the authoring interface and layout, not the building style.
Task: help an artist understand which parts change when editing window recess, without requiring node wiring.
Layout: simplified Buildo top bar with project title "Masonry study", Undo and Save. A large building viewport occupies the left two thirds. A single organized property inspector on the right occupies the remaining third. Header of inspector: "Building controls". Four compact section headings "Shape", "Storeys", "Openings", "Roof & trim"; only Openings is expanded. Within Openings, clearly show "Applies to all 47 windows". Fields with units: Recess 0.25 m, Frame width 0.055 m, Sill projection 0.12 m. One primary action "Preview 47 windows". A small separate disabled affordance under these fields says "Local geometry edits â€” not implemented". Advanced recipe graph is a collapsed disclosure near the inspector bottom. Keep ordinary architectural terminology; no socket names, scope indices or connection controls.
Use exact small but plainly readable persistent banner: "CONCEPT â€” NOT IMPLEMENTED". At bottom of main viewport show a modest status strip "Whole building â€¢ All windows". Do not add fabricated performance metrics or historical evidence badges.
Design a focused primary screen, not a feature inventory. Use spacing, grouping, alignment and type before borders or shadows. Body type 14â€“16 px or equivalent, no more than two fonts. No nested cards, gradients, gratuitous shadows, marketing slogans, feature advertising, fake tools or extra panels. No node diagram visible. One concept only, not a contact sheet.

Target dimensions: 1600 x 1128 landscape desktop app content only, no browser or device chrome. Date anchor 2026-10-18; no visible dates needed.

Task: let an artist identify an opening spatially and propose an edit without scope indices or node wiring. Here the main editing surface is a flat front elevation, not a perspective-only viewport.
Layout: simplified Buildo top bar, project "Masonry study", Undo and Save. Persistent exact banner "CONCEPT â€” NOT IMPLEMENTED". Plain human-readable row labels "Storey 3", "Storey 2", "Ground" down the left and bay column labels "1", "2", "3", "4" above; these alignment guides are clear but subtle, not a spreadsheet grid drawn over every brick. Right area: a smaller three-quarter preview of the SAME building at the top, and below it a contextual section "Selected opening". A short note "Proposed local geometry workflow". A collapsed "Advanced recipe graph" disclosure at bottom.
